Audit 2306: actual generated Foxglove app deployment and ROS/WebSocket delivery

The audit's "published bridge image" wording does not describe production.
Original fix 9ffc87755d09721f9278710c0aca1460c037bb44 and current foxgloveServe
generate a Dockerfile FROM ros:humble which installs the published ROS package
ros-humble-foxglove-bridge, CycloneDDS and socat. This fixture builds that exact
generated recipe through the production deployFoxgloveApp/runWithAgent path.
It does not replace the bridge with a protocol mock or a hand-built test image.

Required execution: existing simulator-python310 job, only matrix.robot == 'go2'
(the existing "ROS Humble simulator dependencies (go2)" Ubuntu 24.04 row).
Keep its shipped requirements and Go2 bridge deadline gate. Do not add this to
containerd-regressions: its driver VM/baseline/watch work already fills its
50-minute budget. No additional matrix row or runner is needed.

After the existing Go setup, install pkg-config and libusb-1.0-0-dev in the
ordinary disposable hosted runner. Docker/buildx, util-linux/unshare, iproute2,
sudo and Python3 are also required. Obtain containerd and runc by extracting
Ubuntu's native packages into an owned directory, without installing/replacing
the runner's Docker daemon packages or changing host service configuration:

  sudo apt-get update --error-on=any
  sudo apt-get install -y pkg-config libusb-1.0-0-dev util-linux iproute2
  runtime="$RUNNER_TEMP/foxglove-runtime-tools"
  mkdir -p "$runtime"
  (
    cd "$runtime"
    apt-get download containerd runc
    for archive in ./*.deb; do dpkg-deb --extract "$archive" root; done
  )
  runtime_path="$runtime/root/usr/bin:$runtime/root/usr/sbin:$runtime/root/bin:$runtime/root/sbin:$PATH"
  env PATH="$runtime_path" python3 .github/scripts/test-foxglove-runtime.py --output "$RUNNER_TEMP/foxglove-runtime"

The coordinator preserves this explicit PATH through sudo into the private
namespace. Commands-package compilation requires CGO_ENABLED=1 for libusb.
The runner's installed Go must match go.mod (the existing Go setup does this).
The full fixture must run once, including both controls; no runtime is skipped
on a failed dependency or unsupported environment.

The coordinator compiles the normal binary and two historical overlays, reuses
one uniquely named production OCI-export buildx builder across fresh isolated
cases, and removes only that builder/config after known namespace drain. The
production Docker builder can start its ordinary hosted BuildKit helper; do not
run this hosted-only namespace entrypoint or OCI-export path on a developer host.
No daemon settings/default builder, image registry publication, host module,
host service or physical device changes are part of the test. Each runtime has
private mount/PID/network namespaces, only loopback networking, a private /run
and /var/lib, an actual ContainerService/AgentService UDS and private containerd.
The local Docker control socket is the only host runtime socket rebound inside.
Docker performs public build-input downloads; the ROS bridge itself has no
external network interface or Cloud credentials. Docker's client also exchanges
registry authorization tokens, so daemon access alone is insufficient. Before
unshare, the owned launch shell opens the original network namespace on FD9.
Inside the private mount namespace it verifies that identity, pins the namespace
with a private bind mount, and closes FD9. Only the Docker PATH wrapper enters
that pinned network namespace; the Agent, ROS publisher and bridge remain in the
private network. The helper verifies original network inode plus private mount/
PID identities and absolute SHA256-pinned Docker/nsenter executables before exec.
It preserves exact argv, private HOME/config, PID namespace and guardian process
group. The original resolver file is copied and privately rebound across /run
replacement. No host resolver, mount, route or daemon configuration is changed.
Portable helper tests check refusal and literal child argv/environment only;
actual setns, registry exchange and deployment require the hosted full gate.

Acceptance requires actual image digest and installed package versions, the
actual generated Dockerfile/config hashes, a negotiated bridge subprotocol,
advertisement of a fresh nonce-specific std_msgs/msg/String channel, and five
strictly increasing independently decoded CDR messages through the real local
WebSocket -> ExecContainer -> socat -> bridge path. Forward cancellation must
drain the CLI while the single deployed bridge remains running. The private
namespace then drains the publisher, app, shim and daemon before work removal.

The named-service descriptor control must build/run the old layout, carry the
real ROS bytes, then fail the observed single-container layout assertion. Current
Agent exec can resolve a single named service, so a fabricated handshake failure
is not required for that control. The old forwarding-target control must have a
real deployed image/packages and fail on the actual absent legacy container name.
Build, package-download, timeout or unrelated RPC errors cannot pass a control.

The whole coordinator has a 20-minute work deadline, with a separate bounded
cleanup allowance; normal runtime is capped at 12 minutes and warm controls at
3 minutes each, all sharing the overall budget. It requires 8 GiB free before
starting. Actual cold duration/peak disk still require hosted measurement before
claiming a measured duration. Reserve 25 minutes for the fixture step
(20-minute work budget, up to 3 minutes bounded cleanup, plus launch margin),
and 15 minutes for package preparation plus the existing Go2 work: a 40-minute outer budget
for the Go2 row only is a conservative upper allocation, not a measured runtime.
The G1 row remains at 15 minutes. Per-compile/per-case timings are emitted in
evidence.json so this allocation can be reduced after the first hosted run.
No additional runner/job is requested.

Retain top-level *.log, evidence.json and overlay *.json, and per-case Dockerfile,
wendy.json, image-digest.txt, installed-packages.txt and containerd.log in the
existing job's small diagnostic artifact. Do not upload docker-config, test
binaries, build cache, images or containerd roots. Unknown drain or ownership
retains the named work/builder, fails acceptance and records cleanup errors.

Portable checks:
  python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p foxglove_runtime_test.py -v
  go test -tags regression_foxglove ./go/internal/cli/commands -run '^TestFoxgloveRuntimeMessageAdmission$' -count=1
  WENDY_FOXGLOVE_EXPORT=NEW_PRIVATE_DIRECTORY go test -tags regression_foxglove ./go/internal/cli/commands -run '^TestFoxgloveExportGeneratedBuild$' -count=1 -v

The last command only exports the production-generated recipe/config. An owner
may build those exact files with an existing ordinary Docker driver for a local
package smoke test; it does not establish real Agent/containerd deployment.
No hardware acceptance, actual robot ROS topic, Foxglove desktop UI, simulator
creation or hosted success follows from portable parser/generation tests.
